name: Tank crew helmet
description: An old-pattern padded canvas cap for tank crews, with thick rolls over the crown to soften knocks against hatches and hull. Earpieces are sewn into the flaps, and a headset lead with a plug trails from the back.
notes: Standing on its ear flaps, front on +z: an olive canvas cap 190 mm across with three dark olive padded rolls front to back over the crown, a padded brow roll round the front and sides, ear flaps with earpieces, a chin strap with a buckle, and the headset lead running back along the floor to its plug, 356 mm long overall with the lead. The lead lies out behind and a soft cap encloses a head-sized box. Slot `head`. Protection is a guess for padding with no hard shell. The headset is not wired to any radio feature. Host for helmet add-ons: `helmet` points at the left side, right side and back of the rim, and a front mount above the brow for goggles. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Mild steel heavy close helm
description: A mild steel helm that closes round the whole head, with a pivoting visor over a chin guard and the tallest comb, three gorget plates and a riveted plate over the chin. With the visor down you look out through a narrow slit and breathe through the slots on the right cheek.
notes: Standing on its gorget, front on +z, 336 mm tall and 240 mm across: a round skull with a comb front to back, 3 flared gorget plates at the foot, a chin plate under a bevor with a centre ridge and five breaths on the right cheek, visor pivots with brass bosses either side, and a riveted reinforcing plate over the bevor. The visor is down with its pointed ridge and the sight slit along its upper edge. Mild steel in `steel-bright`. A helmet is a hollow shell, so the box round the head it encloses is mostly air. Slot `head`; it also covers the eyes and mouth, which the head slot is taken to include. Protection is a guess for a full steel helm graded by weight. The xl size shares the model. Host for helmet add-ons: `helmet` points at the left side, right side and back of the rim; no front mount, because the visor covers the face and nothing that rides there could be used with it. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Mild steel heavy close helm, visor up
description: A mild steel helm that closes round the whole head, with a pivoting visor over a chin guard and the tallest comb, three gorget plates and a riveted plate over the chin. The visor is swung up, so you can see and breathe freely, but the face is open.
notes: Standing on its gorget, front on +z, 336 mm tall and 240 mm across: a round skull with a comb front to back, 3 flared gorget plates at the foot, a chin plate under a bevor with a centre ridge and five breaths on the right cheek, visor pivots with brass bosses either side, and a riveted reinforcing plate over the bevor. The visor is swung up over the brow and the dark padded lining shows through the face opening. Mild steel in `steel-bright`. A helmet is a hollow shell, so the box round the head it encloses is mostly air. The raised visor is a visible state, so it has its own model; Deadvox could later fold the pair into one item with a visor toggle, as its night-vision goggles switch with `wornSwitch`. Protection is a guess and is cut by 15% with the face open, because the eyes and mouth lose cover. The xl size shares the model. Host for helmet add-ons: `helmet` points at the left side, right side and back of the rim; no front mount, because the visor covers the face and nothing that rides there could be used with it. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Mild steel turban helmet
description: A tall, bulbous fluted helmet of mild steel rising to a spike, with hinged ear guards and a nasal bar that slides up and down in a bracket. A modern copy of an old design from the Middle East.
notes: Resting on its ear guards, front on +z, 240 mm across and 352 mm tall with the spike: a broad bowl fluted round its sides narrowing to a collar and a short spike, a raised brow band, broad ear guards hanging from brass hinge rivets each side to the floor, each a plate carrying the bowl's curve down and in over the cheek, and a sliding nasal bar in a bracket at the front with a knob at the top and a leaf-shaped foot. The fluting is vertical; spiral fluting needs a twisted piece the compound family lacks. A helmet is a hollow shell, so the box round the head it encloses is mostly air. Slot `head`; it also covers the mouth through the nasal bar, which the head slot is taken to include. Protection is a guess. The xl and xs sizes share the model.
